_comment: klt erc supply spec for layout/analog/dplus_pullup/dplus_pullup.gds
(issue #222): the analog half of T1 item 11 (power delivery, structural)
for the dplus_pullup leaf. Item 11 is graded from this run's
supply findings -- VPU and VSS each exactly one island, no
erc.missing_tie from a checked tie -- not from the report's overall `status`.
klt erc layout/analog/dplus_pullup/dplus_pullup.gds \
layout/analog/dplus_pullup/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top dplus_pullup --pdk sky130 --format json \
> layout/analog/dplus_pullup/erc-supply-report.json
Layer numbers are sky130A's own drawn layers (the same table gen.py draws
- Supplies are labelled on met1 (68/5): VPU on the PMOS well ring's rail,
VSS on the NMOS ring's rail. The signal pins DP/PU_EN/TRIM0..3 are labelled on
met3 (70/5) and are not declared here: this spec grades supplies only.
- The stack is li1..met3, which is every layer gen.py routes on (rails and
rings on li1/met1, device columns on li1/met1, channel on met2/met3).
poly is declared as the gate role so the antenna table has its denominator;
active_layer makes that denominator poly n diff.
- devices[]: the res_generic_po resistor body (poly_res marker 66/13 over poly) is
a device, not a wire. Without this entry the VPU island would extend
through the resistor into N0..N4/DP and the report would read a rail-to-
signal bridge that is the resistor itself (klt erc 'Device bodies are not
wires').
- ties[]: the n-well tie (nwell 64/20, tap 65/44, wired to li1, net VPU) and
the substrate tie (die extent minus nwell, tap 65/44, wired to li1, net
VSS). sky130's `tap` (65/44) is a tap-only layer -- every shape of it is a
tap, ntap inside the nwell and ptap outside -- so tap_is_dedicated is
declared instead of narrowing with nsdm/psdm: that narrowing removes
nothing from the layout and klt grades it degenerate
(`degenerate_tap_declaration`, skipped work rather than a pass). The ring
is tap + li1, so li1 is the role the tap reaches directly.
